flags: Followed material’s Murphy-to-Rosman mile order, reversing current story and NCDOT’s description. NCDOT’s main route uses Brasstown and local roads near Murphy, so dropped the current implication that US 64 alone covers the entire byway.

Dropped current’s added approximations about two and a half hours, some 200 falls and about 20 feet: the guide gives unhedged figures. Omitted the waterfall count and pavement distance; the latter is broken by PDF column extraction.

Bridal Veil’s dedicated article says pedestrian-only; Highlands article still claims driving behind it. Used the specific article, but no current managing-agency access notice is cached. Practical checked date denotes cache review only.

The cached NCDOT guide is from 2021 and prohibits tractor-trailers and discourages RVs/buses. No current regulation notice is cached; this route-wide limitation needs editorial confirmation before publication.

Route history is supported by secondary Clay County and Chatuge Dam articles; no underlying construction records are cached. The guide’s entirely-marble courthouse claim is narrowed to marble facing because the courthouse article documents a later addition using other materials.
